facts.statement: Platytholus is an extinct dome-headed dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Hell Creek Formation in the United States.
facts.quote: Platytholus is an extinct genus of pachycephalosaurid (dome-headed dinosaur) from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) Hell Creek Formation of the United States.

facts.statement: The genus Platytholus contains only one known species, P. clemensi, which is known from a partial skull.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, P. clemensi, known from a partial skull.

facts.statement: Platytholus had a distinct low, broad, and rectangular dome shape with unique roof-tile-like ornamentation along its sides.
facts.quote: Compared to other pachycephalosaurs, its dome had a distinct low and broad rectangular shape and unique roof-tile like ornamentation along its sides.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen (MOR 2915) was discovered by Jack Horner in the early 2000s in Garfield County, Montana, within the latest Maastrichtian sediments of the Hell Creek Formation.
facts.quote: The Platytholus holotype specimen, MOR 2915, was discovered by paleontologist Jack Horner during the early 2000s in sediments of the Hell Creek Formation, dated to the latest Maastrichtian age of the late Cretaceous period, in Garfield County, Montana.

facts.statement: Platytholus clemensi was formally described as a new genus and species in 2023 by Horner, Goodwin, and Evans.
facts.quote: In 2023, Horner, Mark B. Goodwin and Evans described the specimen as Platytholus clemensi, a new genus and species of pachycephalosaurid.

facts.statement: The genus name Platytholus combines Greek roots meaning "flattened" or "wide" and "small domed hill".
facts.quote: The generic name, "Platytholus", combines the Latinised Greek "platys", meaning "flattened", "wide", or "broad", and "tholos", meaning a "small domed hill".

facts.statement: The species name clemensi honors the American paleontologist William A. Clemens Jr.
facts.quote: The specific name, "clemensi", honors American paleontologist William A. Clemens Jr.

facts.statement: Platytholus was a small, bipedal animal with a solid bone dome covering much of its skull.
facts.quote: As a pachycephalosaur, Platytholus would have been a small bipedal animal with a rounded "dome" structure covering much of the skull and formed of solid bone.

facts.statement: Platytholus incorporated supraorbital and postorbital bones into its dome structure, unlike some relatives where these bones form distinct lobes.
facts.quote: In addition to the frontal and parietal bones that form of the core of the dome in pachycephalosaurs, the supraorbital (above the eyes) and postorbital (above and behind the eyes) bones to the side of the frontals and parietals were incorporated into the dome.

facts.statement: The sides of Platytholus's skull feature unique, sharp-tipped, roof-tile-like ornamentation found nowhere else.
facts.quote: Instead, the sides of the supraorbitals and postorbitals are littered with small and overlapping roof tile-like ornamentation with a compressed shape and sharp tips, unique to Playthtolus.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Platytholus as a derived member of the Pachycephalosaurinae clade.
facts.quote: Horner and colleagues performed a phylogenetic analysis recovered Platytholus as a derived pachycephalosaur within the clade Pachycephalosaurinae.

facts.statement: The exact phylogenetic position of Platytholus is debated and considered weakly supported due to poor preservation of the squamosal ornamentation.
facts.quote: They noted, however, that its phylogenetic position was only weakly supported and limited by the squamosal ornamentation being unpreserved.

facts.statement: Platytholus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Platytholus lived alongside the smaller Sphaerotholus and the larger Pachycephalosaurus.
facts.quote: It was a medium-sized pachycephalosaur, living alongside its smaller relative Sphaerotholus and larger relative Pachycephalosaurus.

facts.statement: The extensive fusion and developed dome state suggest the holotype specimen represents an adult animal.
facts.quote: Based on the incorporation of the developed state of the dome and the extensive fusion within the skull, it is thought to be from an adult animal.
